contents: # Incidents (uhifadhi/incident-module) — what happened in an area: poaching,
# human–wildlife conflict with its fines and compensation, unauthorized
# construction and roadkill, as one record type served to every department that
# needs it.
# NOTHING BELOW IS REQUIRED. Both keys written out have defaults and the tree is
# CLOSED, so an invented key fails at compile time rather than being ignored.
# Delete the whole `incident:` key and a fresh installation still runs.
# WHAT THIS MODULE STANDS ON. Everything that is not about incidents arrives with
# `uhifadhi/uhifadhi`: the per-area catalogue this module's tile is filed in
# (registry), the page frame and the widget mechanics (shell), the people a
# record points at (team), the ground and its overview (area) and the maps the
# plates draw on (atlas).
# `uhifadhi/storage-module` is OPTIONAL here, and the difference from a hard
# requirement is real: incidents only DESCRIBE evidence rows they already hold,
# so a host that never installed it runs every incident screen and simply has no
# /files hub for this module to appear on. Register
# `Uhifadhi\Storage\UhifadhiStorageBundle` and the module registers itself there;
# nothing to configure either way.
# UNTIL THESE PACKAGES ARE ON PACKAGIST an installation names where they come
# from itself. Composer reads `repositories` from the ROOT package only — an
# entry in a dependency's own composer.json is ignored — so they go in the
# application's composer.json, in the form the skeleton's install guide uses:
#   "repositories": [
#       { "type": "vcs", "url": "https://github.com/utafitilabs/uhifadhi" },
#       { "type": "vcs", "url": "https://github.com/utafitilabs/storage-module" },
#       { "type": "vcs", "url": "https://github.com/utafitilabs/incident-module" }
# with `"minimum-stability": "dev"` and `"prefer-stable": true` beside them,
# because composer will not resolve a transitive dev dependency under a stable
# floor. The storage line is needed only where the installation wants incident
# evidence on the Files hub.
incident:
# Which catalogue category the Incidents tile is filed under in every area.
# OPERATIONS: filing the register under `pressure` would say the module
# MEASURES human pressure on the ecosystem; it records the work of answering
# it, which is a different thing.
module_category: operations
# The ISO code the money on an incident — a fine collected, a compensation
# paid — is denominated in. ONE CURRENCY PER DEPLOYMENT, because an area does
# not collect fines in two, and a per-record currency would make every total
# on every screen a question rather than a number.
currency: TZS
# THE KINDS OF INCIDENT THIS DEPLOYMENT RECORDS, and it is deployment
# vocabulary rather than code. LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE: omitting the key installs
# the four kinds and sixteen sub-categories the module ships with, which is
# what almost every installation wants.
# A configured tree REPLACES the shipped one rather than merging with it — a
# half-overridden classification scheme is nobody's scheme — so write the
# whole thing or none of it. Either way it is `incidents:taxonomy:sync` that
# installs it, and the command is idempotent.
#taxonomy:
#    poaching:
#        label: 'Poaching & wildlife crime'
#        # One of the hues incidents.css declares: poach, hwc, comp, mort. A
#        # colour the stylesheet has never heard of renders as an invisible
#        # mark on a map.
#        colour: poach
#        # The departments whose lens puts this kind first. ORDERING ONLY —
#        # it can never gate who may read a row.
#        leads: ['Protection Service']
#        subcategories:
#            snaring:
#                label: snaring
#                # Which way money runs on this kind: fine, compensation, or
#                # ~ for one that carries none — in which case the money
#                # block is ABSENT from the form, not greyed out.
#                money: fine
#                # The term THIS kind promises. A human injury is 72 h and a
#                # construction notice is 14 days; one global SLA would be a
#                # lie about both.
#                term_hours: 72
#                # The fields this kind asks for, in the order the form draws
#                # them.
#                fields: ['Species', 'Snares lifted']
# WHO THE RECORDS POINT AT — and why there is nothing to write here.
# Five columns on this module's tables name a PERSON: who reported the incident,
# who it is assigned to, who acted on the event, who linked it to another, and
# the team member behind a party to it. None of them names an account class; all
# five are mapped to `Uhifadhi\Contracts\Entity\UserInterface`, and the core's
# TeamBundle — the package that actually provides the accounts — states the
# resolution from its own bundle. Whoever knows the answer states it, so an
# ordinary installation writes no doctrine line at all. `bin/console debug:config
# doctrine` shows the one that arrived.
# YOU WRITE A LINE ONLY TO DISAGREE — to name your own account class instead. It
# goes under the `orm:` key ALREADY IN config/packages/doctrine.yaml, beside
# `mappings`. Never as a second `doctrine:` key in that file: Symfony refuses to
# boot with `Duplicate key "doctrine" detected`.
#   doctrine:
#       orm:
#           resolve_target_entities:
#               Uhifadhi\Contracts\Entity\UserInterface: App\Entity\Person
# The application's own configuration wins over a prepended one, so naming your
# class is the whole of it — there is nothing to disable first.
# WHAT THOSE FIVE COLUMNS DO WHEN AN ACCOUNT GOES. They go null and the record
# stays — which is why each of those records also keeps the person's NAME beside
# the relation, written at the time and never rewritten. Removing somebody from
# the team does not un-happen what they reported.
# THEN, in this order:
#   bin/console doctrine:migrations:diff      # your history, your migration
#   bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate
#   bin/console incidents:taxonomy:sync       # the kinds of incident you record
#   bin/console cache:clear
#   bin/console asset-map:compile
# The bundle ships entities, not migrations: the tables are the bundle's, but the
# migration history is yours, and a vendor replaying its own versions into it
# would fight every `diff` you ever run.
# ONE MORE COMMAND, on a daily cron rather than at install time:
# `incidents:close-due` closes every incident that has been resolved for thirty
# days. It is the clock's own move, and it is idempotent.
# Incidents module screens (uhifadhi/incident-module) — the dashboard, the
# library, a case file, the money ledger, the report flow, the taxonomy admin and
# the widget library, all nested under their area:
# /areas/{uuid}/modules/incidents/…
# The addresses are the controllers' own, declared as attributes beside the code
# that answers them. This file is what mounts them, and it is yours: remove the
# import and the screens are gone from `debug:router` with nothing left behind.
incident:
resource: '@UhifadhiIncidentBundle/src/Controller/'
type: attribute
